thread:
sara_sales: Heads-up — POC with NimbusFin. During a ramped concurrency run they hit a bunch of 5xxs and the demo died. Customer is blocking on an SLA and pricing commit until this is stable. Can we triage?

kevin_se: Sorry, saw this. Do we have request IDs or a log snippet?

ana_support: pinged NimbusFin for a few failing request IDs, they sent back one: req=fn-7a3c. Attaching log excerpt below.

ana_support: ```
2026-03-21T14:12:34Z ERROR handler: request=req=fn-7a3c status=503 msg="capacity_exceeded" pool=burstpool node=gpux-34 seq=128
2026-03-21T14:12:34Z WARN  autoscaler: scale_event="delayed" reason="cached_pending>threshold" pending=22 desired=10
2026-03-21T14:12:34Z ERROR runtime: kv_cache_miss=true latency_ms=212
```

mike_oncall: That log looks like the burst pool filled and the autoscaler couldn't spin up nodes fast enough — delayed scale_event. Did the POC request use the high-throughput route?

kevin_se: They set route=standard, concurrency=40, model=nimbus-7b-local (default quant). Standard route maps to shared capacity; burstpool should've handled it but looks saturated.

ryan_infra: Deploy bot shows the autoscaler hit rate limits on the cloud account during that window. I can share the events:

deploy-bot: "autoscaler: scale_up requested=4 granted=2 due_to:quota_limit account=nimbusfin-corp"

ryan_infra: So two problems: (1) external quota constrained new node provisioning, (2) shared burstpool exhausted so requests got backpressured -> 503.

sara_sales: Customer is asking why this happens under a demo load — they expect smooth failover. Also asking if Dedicated capacity is required for demo reliability and what pricing looks like.

kevin_se: Short-term mitigation: reduce concurrency per client, add token-bucket rate limit on the edge to flatten spikes, or route POC to a smaller seq-length profile + quantized model. Long-term: move them to Dedicated or pre-warm reserved burst nodes.

ana_support: Quick rollback option: pin to a lower-cost variant that uses fewer GPU resources while we stabilize. Example config: ```json
{"model_variant":"nimbus-7b-8bit","route":"dedicated-fallback","max_concurrency":12}```

mike_oncall: For immediate triage I recommend: 1) enable temporary per-api-key qps cap (e.g., 10 rps), 2) flip cache_policy to "warm_prefixes" for their prompt set, 3) re-run the ramp and collect flamegraphs.

sara_sales: Can we give NimbusFin a clear ask list so their engineers can help? They want next steps and whether we can guarantee no 5xx during the next demo.

kevin_se: I'll send them a checklist:
- throttle spike: implement client-side concurrency cap 12
- switch to nimbus-7b-8bit for demo runs
- set route to dedicated-fallback or a reserved pool (we can allocate small reserved pool for a week)
- share failing req IDs and sample payloads

ana_support: Also flag to infra: can you request a temporary quota bump for their account so autoscaler can provision on scale_up? This is the blocker.

ryan_infra: On it. Filed cloud quota request (case 987654). ETA ~2 business hours. I'll also add a temporary policy to allow extra burst nodes from our backup pool if quota not granted.

deploy-bot: "policy:backup_burstpool attached to account=nimbusfin-corp expires=2026-03-22T02:00:00Z"

mike_oncall: If the backup pool kicks in, we should still watch tail latency — backpressure could still appear when KV cache misses spike. Keep an eye on cache hit rate and sequence lengths.

sara_sales: Pricing question from NimbusFin: they asked if a short-term reserved window (1 week) has a prorated Dedicated fee or if we can provide a demo credit. What should I say?

kevin_se: For deals under evaluation we can offer a temporary reserved commit with pro-rated billing or a demo credit depending on the contract team. I'll loop in AMs, but be conservative and say "we can provide a short trial reserved pool with limited discount; full Dedicated pricing applies for long-term commits."

ana_support: Customer also sent a security ask: their infosec won't sign off without SOC2 + VPC option. That might push them to Private. I've shared our SOC2 cert and VPC architecture doc via secure link.

sara_sales: Noted. I told them Private is an option but has longer lead time. They understand but want the POC stable in the meantime.

ryan_infra: Operational note: after quota bump and backup pool activation, we should run a controlled replay of their traffic at target QPS to validate failover. I can coordinate a 30-min window.

mike_oncall: Agreed. During the replay collect: /metrics autoscaler_events, /logs requestId fn-* , kv_cache_hit_rate, per-node gpu_util. If we still see >1% 5xx, escalate to model-team for a lighter kernel or batching change.

kevin_se: I'll draft the message to NimbusFin engineers with the checklist + staged plan and proposed time slot for replay.

sara_sales: Thanks all. Can someone drop a one-line summary I can send to their CTO?

ana_support: "Summary: 5xxs caused by burstpool saturation + cloud quota limits delaying autoscaler. Short-term: limit concurrency, switch to 8-bit variant, enable backup burstpool. Mid-term: reserve a small Dedicated pool or Private deployment for full SLA. Infra requested quota bump; we will run a controlled replay once uplifted." :thumbsup:

sara_sales: Perfect. Sending now. Will update when NimbusFin confirms replay time.

kevin_se: Follow-up: if they want zero risk for a live demo we should spin a tiny Dedicated fleet for that demo window — cost estimate ~ $X/day, will confirm with finance/AM.

ryan_infra: Cloud quota update: approved for +6 nodes for 4 hours (temp). Pushing patch to enable backup_burstpool now.

deploy-bot: "autoscaler: patch applied -> allow_backup_burstpool=true"

mike_oncall: We'll run the replay at 2026-03-22T15:00 UTC. Kevin, Sara — I'll own the runbook and watch ops channel.

sara_sales: Thanks team — closing the loop.

kevin_se: Keep the req IDs if anything recurs.

ana_support: will archive logs to the ticket and follow up with NimbusFin post-demo.
